module: LuLPeg: third-party library (Pierre-Yves Gérardy, "Romantic WTF" license), a pure-Lua port of LPeg (Parsing Expression Grammars by Roberto Ierusalimschy). The file is a bundle of several internal submodules (util, compiler, datastructures, re, charsets, evaluator, printers, analyzer, locale, match, factorizer, API, constructors, init, compat, optimizer) and ends with `return require"init"`: require("libs/LuLPeg/lulpeg") directly returns the LL object (equivalent to the lpeg module) with the `re` submodule. Used to write text parsers (grammars, patterns, captures).
usage:
local lpeg = require("libs/LuLPeg/lulpeg")
local P, C, R = lpeg.P, lpeg.C, lpeg.R
local number = C(R"09"^1)
print(number:match("123abc")) --> "123"
notes: The file declares no global function to document: the public API is that of the returned object (LL), built by the submodules.

Main LL API (read from the code): P, S, R, V, B, L (pattern constructors); C, Cs, Ct, Cc, Cg, Cb, Cf, Cmt, Cp, Carg (captures); match, dmatch (execution), ispattern, type, locale, pprint, cprint, evaluate, compile, resetptcache; version() returns "0.12", luversion() "0.1.0"; setmaxstack is a stub with no effect; new(options) creates an independent instance; global(env) and register(env) install lpeg/re in an environment; LL.re submodule (textual grammars).
Lua operators are overloaded on patterns: p1 * p2 (sequence), p1 + p2 (choice), p1 - p2 (difference), p^n (repetition), -p (negation), #p ("and" predicate), p / x (replacement capture).
The returned table has an `__index` field pointing to itself, so patterns also have the methods (e.g. pattern:match(s)).

P.desc: Builds a pattern (literal string, number of characters, boolean, grammar table, function).

S.desc: Character set pattern (one character among those of the string).

V.desc: Reference to a grammar rule (non-terminal variable).

C.desc: Simple capture: returns the substring that matches the pattern.

Cs.desc: Substitution string capture (inner captures replace the matching text).

Ct.desc: Table capture: groups the pattern's captures into a table.

Cc.desc: Constant capture: produces the given values without consuming text.

Cp.desc: Position capture: returns the current position in the subject.

Cb.desc: Back capture: returns the value of a previous named group.

Cf.desc: Fold capture: applies an accumulating function over the captures; the function is required (assert).

Cmt.desc: Match-time capture: a function decides at run time whether the pattern succeeds; the function is required (assert).

Carg.desc: Capture of extra argument n of match (n between 1 and 200).

match.desc: match(pattern, subject, init, ...): applies the pattern to the subject and returns the captures (or the end position), nil on failure.

dmatch.desc: Like match but in debug mode (prints traces).

re.desc: re submodule: patterns written in textual syntax (re.compile, re.match, re.find, re.gsub...).
